title: Reduce host-side pipeline overhead: memory-copy paths, CPU->GPU handoff, and threadpool contention
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Host CPU overhead for short and mixed-length requests remains a dominant contributor to end-to-end p50/p95 latency. We observe excessive CPU time spent in: (1) staging and pinning host buffers, (2) synchronous cudaMemcpy and memory copy stalls, (3) frequent kernel launch/teardown from many small attention kernels, and (4) threadpool contention between prefill/kv-cache population and decode worker pools.

Goal: Reduce host-side overhead delivered to the serving runtime so that CPU utilization for prefill and small-decode workloads drops, memory-copy stalls are minimized, and tail latency improves for both short-chat and single-turn generation. Approach combines: pinned/pooled host buffers (cudaHostAlloc/cudaHostRegister), persistent pinned staging ring, batched/merged async memcpy submissions to dedicated CUDA streams, single-submission fused kernel paths for attention-prefill where applicable, and scheduling changes to reduce contention in the host threadpool (dedicated I/O thread per GPU + cooperative worker queues).

Scope: This ticket covers design, prototype, and rollout for the host-side changes described below; kernel fusion/selection changes will be implemented as compatible variants in a follow-on (see sub_issues).
acceptance_criteria: Reduce average host CPU sys+user time per 1k short requests by >=30% measured on a 8xA100 test cluster (same load generator as perf/short-chat-bench)
Reduce median host-to-device memcpy latency for 512B-8KB payloads by >=40% across benchmarks (use io/transfer dashboard)
p99 end-to-end latency for 16-token responses improves by >=15% without increasing GPU cycle cost per token
No regressions in throughput for large-batch prefill (>1024 tokens) beyond 5% compared to baseline
Rollout plan validated via canary on dedicated pool and metrics tracked in runtime-1.21 canary dashboard
notes: 2026-03-02: Spike completed. Microbenchmarks show 2.2x speedup for small memcpy paths when using a persistent pinned buffer pool vs ad-hoc cudaHostAlloc + cudaMemcpy.
2026-03-04: Decision to prefer cudaHostRegister when possible for buffers allocated by Rust arena; fallback to cudaHostAlloc for external buffers coming from user code.

2026-03-05: Implemented prototype of 'staging ring' (single-threaded producer) that aggregates small prefill copies into larger batched device writes. Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3112 (WIP)

2026-03-06: Threadpool profiling shows lock contention around the shared work-stealing deque used by prefill and decode worker pools. Proposed change: split pools by phase and add a per-GPU dedicated I/O submit thread to isolate copy/submit work from decoder CPU-heavy tasks.

2026-03-07: Kernel-change tradeoff: we can reduce kernel launches by fusing small-attention windows into a single kernel for short sequences, but this increases register pressure and may slightly increase per-token GPU time. Will gate fused kernel behind runtime config and model capability matrix.

2026-03-08: PRs and artifacts: design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/host-path-optimizations, perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/runtime/host-path, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3112, follow-up PR for threadpool changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124
2026-03-09: Security review: no secrets in host buffer pool; KMS unaffected. security_team pinged for visibility (security_review_required=false).

2026-03-10: Review feedback from infra: prefer using dedicated pinned buffer pool managed by allocator to avoid fragmentation; also recommend exposing counters for pinned allocations to prevent leaks in long-running private deployments.
2026-03-11: Blocking item: reproduce threadpool contention with dockerized perf harness — current repro works on baremetal but not in CI runner. investigating isolation differences.
